content.comment_body: Hello, I'm experiencing an issue with my configuration. I want output Q1 to activate when the analog input I7 reads 1000K Ohms through an LDR, and deactivate Q1 when it reads 20K Ohms. I'm unsure how to monitor the instantaneous value at I7. Could someone advise? Thank you.

The analog input on the basic module of [product_name] receives a voltage signal (0-10V) which it converts to a range, generally 0 to 1000 units. It does not directly detect resistance values, so connecting an LDR directly would not work for evaluation purposes. Attached is a circuit suggestion featuring an LDR model 'A 1060'. You will need to determine switching thresholds by measuring voltage or by monitoring the AI1 values through online observation or the module’s display.
Thanks for your schematic! I’ll test it.

I've resolved the issue since I managed to read the current value on the display by using the arrow keys. When trying your schematic, I couldn't view the updated display on my device and wasn't sure why. Regardless, I was able to fix it, thank you for your help.

analysis.insight_summary: The user had trouble monitoring the real-time analog value on input I7 while using a light-dependent resistor with [product_name]. The discussion highlighted the key UX point that the module reads voltage, not resistance, requiring users to understand both the input signal and how to observe live data from the device. The forum revealed common confusion around sensor compatibility and real-time signal monitoring.
analysis.user_expectations: Users expect to connect an LDR directly to an analog input and easily view real-time input values via the device interface for configuration and troubleshooting purposes.
